Managing anxiety with OCD can feel overwhelming, but there are strategies that may help. Many people benefit from working with a mental health professional trained in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), a therapy specifically designed for OCD. It gradually helps you face fears without engaging in compulsions, reducing anxiety over time. Mindfulness practices, grounding techniques, and learning to label intrusive thoughts as just thoughts can also be useful tools.

It's important to remember that anxiety often spikes before it gets better, and progress isn't always linear. Be patient with yourself. If you're not already connected with a therapist or counselor, reaching out to one can make a meaningful difference. You can also contact the International OCD Foundation or a crisis line like 988 (in the U.S.) if you need immediate support. You don't have to navigate this alone.
